2026-12-05.title: First Saturday of Annunciation
2026-12-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
2026-12-05.verse: Jesus said to him, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
theo: Paul asks the Galatians: did you receive the Spirit by works of the law or by believing what you heard? “Those who believe are the descendants of Abraham.” Faith is the open hand that receives God's gift.

On the road to Jerusalem three would-be followers meet Jesus. To one he says, “The Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head”; to another, “Let the dead bury their own dead”; to the third, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” Elisha burned his plough to follow Elijah. Discipleship is wholehearted; the Lord who comes at Christmas asks for an undivided heart.
outline: Ask: what makes you look back when following Christ?
We receive the Spirit by believing.
Point 2 · Nowhere to lay his head
Following Jesus means trusting, not securing.
Elisha burned his plough; disciples do not look back.
“I will follow you, Lord, without looking back.”
live: Give up one thing that keeps pulling you back from God.
Pray the Rosary today with Mary, the perfect disciple.
2026-12-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, you had nowhere to lay your head. Give me a faith that follows you without delay and without looking back, like Mary your mother. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we receive, not earn. We come with open hands, as children of Abraham by faith, and Christ gives himself freely.

quick: We receive the Spirit by faith.

2026-12-05.question: What makes me look back?

family.explain: Jesus wants us to follow him right away, not later. When we plough a field we look ahead, not behind.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who keeps postponing their return to God.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing have we been putting off that we can do this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us to follow you without delay. Gather us now, give us faith like Abraham, and help us put our hand to the plough without looking back. Amen.
share: Paul says we receive the Spirit by faith, not by works (Galatians 3:2). Do I sometimes try to earn God's love?
What am I postponing that God is asking me to do now?
What in my past still makes me look back instead of forward?
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim salvation as God's free gift.
For those who feel they are never good enough, that they may know God's love.
For young people choosing their vocation, that they may follow Christ generously.
For those weighed down by the past, that they may be healed and look forward with hope.
For our prayer group, that we may not delay our conversion.
pm.close: Lord God, you justified Abraham by faith and you call us to follow your Son. Free us from fear and delay, and make us faithful disciples who never look back. Amen.

illus: An old farmer in Kuttanad used to tell young men learning to plough: “Fix your eye on a coconut tree at the end of the field and walk towards it. If you look at your feet or behind you, the line will bend.” Jesus is the tree at the end of our field.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul asks the Galatians a sharp question: did you receive the Spirit by doing the works of the law, or by believing what you heard? (Galatians 3:2). Some teachers were telling them that faith in Christ was not enough; they also had to keep the whole law of Moses.

Paul answers by pointing to Abraham: he believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness; so those who believe are the descendants of Abraham (Galatians 3:6–7). Salvation is a gift received by faith, not a wage earned by our performance.

This is good news for those who feel they are never good enough. We do not earn God's love by our fasting, our devotions or our donations. These are responses to love already given. The Christmas fast is not a way to buy God's favour; it is a way to open our hands to receive the Gift.

In the Gospel three people want to follow Jesus. To the first he says: foxes have holes, and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head. To the second, who wants first to bury his father: let the dead bury their own dead. To the third, who wants to say goodbye: no one who puts a hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God (Luke 9:57–62).

These are hard words. Jesus is not against burying our parents or saying goodbye to family. He is warning against delay. Many of us say: I will pray more after the exams, after the wedding, after I retire. Jesus says: now.

A farmer ploughing with oxen must look forward. If he keeps looking back, the furrow becomes crooked. Faith also needs a forward gaze: forgiving the past, not living in regret, trusting God for the future.
What is God asking you to do that you keep postponing? A reconciliation, a confession, a habit of prayer, a generous act? This Nombu, put your hand to the plough and do not look back. Amen.
kids: Children, a farmer who looks back cannot plough a straight line. When Jesus asks you to do something good, do it right away!

intro: Faith receives the Spirit; discipleship does not look back.

sub: Abraham believed and was reckoned righteous.
q: And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
points.apply: Make an act of faith today.

sub: Elisha left everything to follow Elijah.
A real decision has no way back.
q: He returned from following him, took the yoke of oxen, and slaughtered them; using the equipment from the oxen, he boiled their flesh, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he set out and followed Elijah, and became his servant.
Jesus said to him, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
points.apply: Give up one thing that pulls you back.

q: Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?
Then he said to them all, “If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.”
points.apply: Pray the Rosary with Mary today.

concl: The Lord who comes asks for an undivided heart.
Let us follow without looking back.
